messages.content: Distributed training uses multiple computing devices to collaboratively train a machine learning model.
Data parallelism places a copy of the model on each device and trains each copy on different subsets of the data.
Model parallelism splits a model across multiple devices so that different parts of the model execute on different hardware.
Gradient accumulation combines gradients from several micro-batches before performing an optimizer update.
LoRA fine-tunes a model by training small low-rank matrices while keeping most pretrained parameters frozen.
Why is mixed precision training useful?
Mixed precision training reduces memory usage and can improve throughput by using lower-precision numerical formats where appropriate.
GPU memory bandwidth measures how quickly data can be transferred between GPU memory and its compute units.
All-reduce aggregates values such as gradients across multiple devices and returns the combined result to every participating device.
